Files: `/root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/test/fake-dom.mjs` (the fake DOM + fake fetch harness, not a test file) and `/root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/test/app-behaviour.test.mjs` (split into `app-list.test.mjs` / `app-actions.test.mjs` if over 400 lines). node:test + node:assert/strict, Node 22 built-ins only. Skill to load: tdd-workflow (if unavailable, follow these rules). Spec (source of truth): `/root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/.team/notes/spec.md`, section "Page". Read public/app.js first. Do NOT edit anything outside these test files. Run: `cd /root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0 && node --test test/app-*.test.mjs` (`node --test test/` is broken on Node 22). If a failure is a real spec violation in app.js, keep the test and report the repro; never weaken it. Project rules: no console.log; files under 400 lines; functions under 50 lines; exact equality on all texts, URLs, headers and bodies. Fake DOM (fake-dom.mjs), only what the spec allows the script to use — anything else must be absent so misuse throws: - `FakeText` node {nodeType: 3, data}. `FakeElement` {tagName (uppercase), id, childNodes array, listeners map, `type`, `value`, `disabled` (false), plus `textContent` getter (concat of descendant text) / setter (replaces children with one text node, or none for '')}, `append(...nodes)` (strings become FakeText), `replaceChildren(...nodes)` (same conversion), `addEventListener(type, fn)`, and a test-only `dispatch(type)` that creates an event `{type, target, defaultPrevented:false, preventDefault(){this.defaultPrevented=true}}`, calls listeners, and returns the event. For select elements, `value` defaults to the value of the first option child when not set (like a browser) — keep simple: if never assigned, getter returns first child option's value or ''. - `document` = { getElementById(id), createElement(tag) } only. Pre-create elements: form#booking-form, select#room, input#title(type text), input#date(type date), input#start, input#end (time), button#book (submit), input#filter-date (date), button#show-all, ul#booking-list, p#error. - Fake `fetch(url, options)`: records each call `{url, options}` and returns a promise the test controls: `calls[i].respond(status, bodyValueOrRawText)` resolves a Response-like `{status, json(){...}}` where json() resolves with the parsed body (or rejects for raw invalid JSON text); `calls[i].fail()` rejects with TypeError. A 204 respond with json() rejecting (no body). - `loadApp()` creates context via `vm.createContext({document, fetch, ...nothing else... })` — also provide no `window`/`setTimeout`; run `new vm.Script(appJsText).runInContext(ctx)`; return {doc elements, fetchCalls, flush} where `flush()` awaits several macrotask ticks (`await new Promise(r => setImmediate(r))` a few times) so promise chains settle. Helper `listTexts()` → array of each li's description: for each li, assert/return `[childNodes.length, first child nodeType, first child data, second child tagName/type/textContent]`. Tests (each separate): 1. Load order: right after running the script synchronously (before flush), fetch was called exactly twice: first `/api/rooms`, second `/api/bookings` (list fetch starts without waiting for rooms reply). Options for GETs: either undefined or without method other than GET. 2. Rooms: respond 200 `{"rooms":["Aurora","Borealis","Cosmos"]}` → #room has 3 OPTION children, value and textContent each the name, in order. Rooms error 500 `{"error":"internal error"}` → #error text `internal error`, #room has 0 children. Rooms error with body `{"error":5}` → `Request failed.`. Rooms fetch rejects → `Could not reach the server.`, #room empty. Rooms 200 with invalid JSON raw text → treated as no reply → `Could not reach the server.`. 3. List render: respond bookings `[{id:1,room:'Aurora',title:'x',date:'2026-11-03',start:'09:00',end:'10:00'}]` → #booking-list has one LI with exactly 2 child nodes: a text node with data exactly `2026-11-03 09:00-10:00 Aurora: x` and a BUTTON with type `button` and textContent `Cancel`. Order follows the reply's order (give 2 bookings in non-sorted order; the list must keep reply order). Empty → one LI whose only child is a text node `No bookings.`. A successful list fetch leaves #error untouched (set errorBox.textContent='keep' before responding; still 'keep'). 4. List errors: error status 400 `{"error":"date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date"}` → #error shows it, list unchanged (pre-populated from an earlier successful fetch). Rejected fetch → `Could not reach the server.`, list unchanged. Error status with non-object body `[]` → `Request failed.`. 5. Stale list fetch: trigger two list fetches (initial + change event on #filter-date after setting value '2026-11-03'); respond to the LATER one first with bookings A, then the EARLIER with bookings B → list shows A. Then repeat with the earlier one failing (reject) or returning an error status after the later succeeded → #error unchanged and list unchanged. Also the earlier responding first then later → final is later's result. 6. Filter URL: set #filter-date value '2026-11-03' then dispatch 'change' → new fetch url exactly `/api/bookings?date=2026-11-03`. Dispatch 'input' → no new fetch. With value '' change → `/api/bookings`. Value passed unchanged (set value 'a b&c' → url `/api/bookings?date=a b&c`). 7. Show all: with filter value '2026-11-03', click #show-all (dispatch 'click') → filter value '' and exactly one new fetch with url `/api/bookings`; no 'change' listener invoked (exactly one fetch added). 8. Booking submit: set room select value 'Cosmos' (after rooms loaded), title ' Plan ', date '2026-11-03', start '09:00', end '10:00'; dispatch 'submit' on the form → event.defaultPrevented true; #book.disabled true; fetch call url `/api/bookings`, options.method 'POST', options.headers deep-equal `{"Content-Type":"application/json"}` exactly (only that header), JSON.parse(options.body) deep-equal `{room:'Cosmos',title:' Plan ',date:'2026-11-03',start:'09:00',end:'10:00'}` (title NOT trimmed) with exactly those 5 keys. Second submit while disabled → defaultPrevented true and no new fetch. Respond 201 with the booking → #book.disabled false, #title value '', other fields unchanged, #error '' (pre-set to 'old'), and a new list fetch made (`/api/bookings`, or with ?date when filter set). Respond 409 `{"error":"room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00"}` → #error exactly that, #book enabled, title kept, no list fetch. Reject → `Could not reach the server.`, enabled, no list fetch. 400 with body `{"message":"x"}` → `Request failed.`. Empty fields are sent as '' (the script never checks fields itself: submit with all empty → fetch still made). "Book enabled before anything else happens": in the 201 case, check that at the moment the new list fetch is called, #book.disabled is already false (record disabled state inside fetch mock). 9. Cancel: list with booking id 7; click its Cancel button → button.disabled true, fetch url `/api/bookings/7`, options.method 'DELETE'. Respond 204 → button.disabled false, #error '' (pre-set 'old'), list fetched again. Respond 404 `{"error":"booking not found"}` → #error `booking not found`, list fetched again. Reject → `Could not reach the server.`, button enabled, no list fetch. 10. Plain text: a title with `x` appears verbatim in the text node (already in 3) and no element child other than the button. Report back: files written, test count, pass/fail summary, and any app.js spec violations with exact repro.

content.content: 1 # Meeting-room booking app — full spec (verbatim from the user; final, no questions allowed) 2 3 Constraints: Use only Node.js built-ins (no npm install). Node v22. Do not use the Fable model. 4 5 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. 6 7 ## Server 8 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 9 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 14 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 15 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 16 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 17 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 18 19 ## API 20 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 21 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. 22 - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. 23 - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 24 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 25 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. 26 - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. 27 - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. 28 - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). 29 - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. 30 - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. 31 - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. 32 33 ## Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 34 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 35 2. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 37 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 38 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 39 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 40 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 41 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 42 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 43 10. The booking overlaps a booking of the same room on the same date, that is each of the two starts before the other ends (a booking may start exactly when another ends): 409 `room is already booked from to `, with the start and end of the overlapping booking that starts earliest. 44 - No field except `title` is trimmed or changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid. 45 46 ## Page 47 - `GET /` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` and the page. `GET /app.js` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/javascript; charset=utf-8` and the page's script. 48 - The page loads the script with a `

I wrote the fake DOM harness and 34 behaviour tests for `public/app.js`. All 34 pass with `node --test test/app-*.test.mjs`, and I found no spec violations in `app.js`.

I didn't load the tdd-workflow skill, so I followed its rules directly. The tests were written after reading `app.js`, not before it.

- **Files:** `test/fake-dom.mjs` is the harness. It holds the fake elements, the fake `document` and the controllable fetch, and `loadApp()` runs `app.js` in `node:vm` with only `document` and `fetch` in the context. I split the tests in two to stay under 400 lines: `test/app-list.test.mjs` has 22 tests and `test/app-actions.test.mjs` has 12.
- **Reply shape:** The task's example showed the bookings reply as a bare array. The spec says the reply is `{"bookings": [...]}`, so I used the spec shape. In the list-error test, a body of `[]` is only used as a non-object error body.
- **Cross-realm values:** `options.headers` comes from inside the vm context. The harness exports a `plain()` helper that round-trips it through JSON so `deepEqual` works.
- **Extra coverage:** I added two cases you didn't list. One checks that an earlier list error arriving before the later reply is also ignored. The other checks that the post-201 refetch keeps the `?date=` filter.
- **Bash permission:** The first Bash call, with a `grep`/`tail` pipe, was denied. I re-ran the bare test command and it was allowed.
